note: How the scenario moves a rating. Read by src/lib/score.js. Every rule here fires on data the tool already holds: the fetched weapon stats, the game own tags, or fields curated in items.json. Nothing here is a hand written per item list. A rule states a delta in points, where roughly 14 points is one tier, or scales one from a number the game publishes. Every rule must carry a `say`, because a score that cannot explain itself is a score nobody should trust. And every rule must fire on something that actually varies with the scenario, which is the test the armour rules failed.
whyThereAreNoArmourRules: There were five, added in 1.10.0 and removed in 1.13.0, and they were the wrong altitude. Measured on the Automaton front, 48 of 51 primaries shared one of two identical armour readings and 42 of them lost a tier for it. A rule that fires the same way on 94% of a population is not telling you anything about any of them. The deeper error: a community tier already prices in what an item is for. Voters know an assault rifle does not open a Hulk, so the Liberator's B on bots is a B given that it is a chaff gun, and penalising it again charges twice for one fact. The test to apply to any replacement is whether the thing it fires on actually varies with the scenario. Armour reach per item does not; it is constant, and only the front and difficulty move it, which moves every primary together. That makes it a loadout property. src/lib/squad.js already had this right, asking whether anyone in the squad carries AP 4 or better rather than judging each weapon alone, and that is the shape armour scoring should come back in.
sourceOfHazardWording: The hazard mechanics quoted in these sentences come from the helldivers-2/json community dataset, MIT licensed. They are the game's own descriptions, not our guesses.

rules.name: Heat weapons fire longer · extreme cold
rules.say: Extreme cold slows heat buildup, so this fires longer before it overheats.

rules.name: Heat weapons overheat sooner · intense heat
rules.say: Intense heat speeds up heat buildup, so this overheats sooner.

rules.name: Fast firing weapons slow down · extreme cold
rules.say: Extreme cold lowers rate of fire, and weapons that fire 700 rounds a minute or more feel it most.

rules.name: Stratagems unreliable · ion storms
rules.say: Ion storms disable stratagems from time to time, so this may not arrive when you call it.

rules.name: Carried weapons help · ion storms
rules.say: Ion storms disable stratagems from time to time. Weapons and grenades you carry keep working.

rules.name: Marksman rifles less useful · sandstorms
rules.say: Sandstorms reduce visibility, so long range weapons are less useful. Each storm lasts about 3 minutes.

rules.name: Long range support weapons less useful · sandstorms
rules.say: Sandstorms reduce visibility, so long range weapons are less useful. Each storm lasts about 3 minutes.
rules.judgement: No published stat marks a support weapon as long range, so we tag them by hand. Projectile speed does not separate them: lasers read 1300, assault rifles 820.

rules.name: Shotguns and SMGs help · sandstorms
rules.say: Sandstorms reduce visibility, so most fights happen at close range.

rules.name: Marksman rifles less useful · blizzards
rules.say: Blizzards reduce visibility while they last, so long range weapons are less useful.

rules.name: Long range support weapons less useful · blizzards
rules.say: Blizzards reduce visibility while they last, so long range weapons are less useful.
rules.judgement: No published stat marks a support weapon as long range, so we tag them by hand. Projectile speed does not separate them: lasers read 1300, assault rifles 820.

rules.name: Shotguns and SMGs help · blizzards
rules.say: Blizzards reduce visibility, so fights start at closer range.

rules.name: Marksman rifles less useful · thick fog
rules.say: Thick fog slightly reduces visibility, so long range weapons are a little less useful.

rules.name: Long range support weapons less useful · thick fog
rules.say: Thick fog slightly reduces visibility, so long range weapons are a little less useful.
rules.judgement: No published stat marks a support weapon as long range, so we tag them by hand. Projectile speed does not separate them: lasers read 1300, assault rifles 820.

rules.name: Weapons with a stationary reload less useful · tremors
rules.say: Tremors stun everyone nearby. This weapon reloads standing still, so a tremor can stun you mid reload.

rules.name: Sentries, emplacements and mines less useful · tremors
rules.say: Tremors stun everything on the ground, you included while you set this up.

rules.name: Fire weapons less useful · fire tornadoes
rules.say: Fire tornadoes already spread fire across the map. Adding your own makes it harder to stay out of the flames.

rules.name: Armour passives weaker · acid storms
rules.say: Acid storms reduce armour for everyone while they last, so armour passives are worth a little less.

rules.name: Durable damage helps · Terminids
rules.say: Big Terminids are mostly tough flesh. Weapons with high durable damage keep most of their damage against it.

rules.name: Weak against tough flesh · Terminids
rules.say: Almost all of this weapon's damage is standard damage, which does little to tough flesh like a Charger's rear or a Spewer's sack.

rules.name: Slow handling hurts · Terminids
rules.say: Low ergonomics makes the barrel slow to follow your aim. Hunters close in fast.

rules.name: Big magazines help · Illuminate
rules.say: Crushers regenerate when the damage pauses. A big magazine keeps the damage going.

rules.name: Small magazines less useful · Illuminate
rules.say: Crushers regenerate when the damage pauses, and reloading every few shots gives them that pause.

rules.name: Demolition force 40+ helps · Structure demolition, Blitz
rules.say: Demolition force 40 or more closes bug holes and fabricators from outside, without spending a stratagem. These missions are built around destroying structures.

rules.name: Objective closers help · Structure demolition, Blitz
rules.say: This closes objectives from your own kit, so you spend fewer stratagems on them. These missions are built around destroying structures.

rules.name: Support weapons less useful · Carry
rules.say: Carrying the objective takes your hands, so this stays on your back for most of the mission.

rules.name: Smoke helps · Escort
rules.say: Smoke blocks enemy line of sight along the civilians' route.

rules.name: Sentries, emplacements and mines help · Eradicate, Hold the line
rules.say: You defend one area for the whole mission, so anything you place there keeps working the entire time.

rules.name: The Cremator helps · Eradicate, Hold the line
rules.say: You defend one area while enemies keep coming. The Cremator's 500 rounds, fed from your backpack, cover the approach with fire.
rules.judgement: The Cremator suits holding one position against large groups. This rule skips the front: the community tier already rates fire per front. Named by hand, since no published stat marks a backpack fed flamethrower.

rules.name: Anti-tank helps · High value target
rules.say: These missions count only a set number of named heavy enemies, and anti-tank is what kills them.

rules.name: Fast demolition helps · Blitz
rules.say: You have 12 minutes to destroy every structure on the map. Demolition force 40 or more closes each one from outside, with no throw to line up.

rules.name: Sidearms help · Carry
rules.say: You carry an objective for most of this mission. A one handed weapon can fire while you carry it.

rules.name: SMGs help · Carry
rules.say: You carry an objective for most of this mission. A one handed weapon can fire while you carry it.

rules.name: Stealth advised · Automatons, 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: A silenced weapon is heard at 13 metres instead of 100. You can kill a sentry without alerting the rest of the base.
rules.source: The 5 suppressed weapons. The wiki lists Suppressed in each weapon's infobox, and its Stealth page gives the audible range as 13 metres.
rules.judgement: 1 or 2 players only: solo from Suicide Mission, or 2 players from Impossible. A full squad on Super Helldive plays loud and does fine. Grows to about a tier for 1 player on Super Helldive.

rules.name: Quieter weapons draw fewer patrols · Automatons, 1 or 2 players, peril 28+
rules.say: This weapon is quieter than most and draws fewer patrols. With 1 or 2 players, nobody covers you while you deal with them.
rules.source: The game's own noise template for each weapon, read from its weapon data: small, medium, large or huge.
rules.judgement: The size is ours: about a quarter of a tier at solo Super Helldive. 1 or 2 players only.

rules.name: Loud weapons draw patrols · Automatons, 1 or 2 players, peril 28+
rules.say: Every shot from this is heard up to 100 metres away and draws patrols. With 1 or 2 players, nobody covers you while you deal with them.
rules.judgement: The size is ours. Medium is the most common class, and weapons with no class in the game file are counted here too. 1 or 2 players only, from solo on Impossible or 2 players on Helldive.
rules.source: The game's own noise template for each weapon, read from its weapon data: small, medium, large or huge.

rules.name: Very loud weapons draw patrols · Automatons, 1 or 2 players, peril 28+
rules.say: This weapon is heard further than most and draws patrols from far away. With 1 or 2 players, nobody covers you while you deal with them.
rules.source: The game's own noise template for each weapon, read from its weapon data: small, medium, large or huge.
rules.judgement: The size is ours: under a tier at solo Super Helldive. Large and huge classes: the Autocannon, the Anti-Materiel Rifle, the expendable and recoilless launchers. 1 or 2 players only.

rules.name: Quieter weapons draw fewer patrols · Terminids, Illuminate, 1 or 2 players, peril 28+
rules.say: This weapon is quieter than most and starts fewer breaches and Watcher alerts. With 1 or 2 players, nobody covers you while you deal with it.
rules.source: The game's own noise template for each weapon. helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth: every faction detects by sound, then sight.
rules.judgement: Six tenths of the Automaton rule, like the other stealth rules on these fronts.

rules.name: Loud weapons draw patrols · Terminids, Illuminate, 1 or 2 players, peril 28+
rules.say: Every shot from this is heard up to 100 metres away and can start a breach or a Watcher alert. With 1 or 2 players, nobody covers you while you deal with it.
rules.source: The game's own noise template for each weapon. helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth: every faction detects by sound, then sight.
rules.judgement: Six tenths of the Automaton rule, like the other stealth rules on these fronts.

rules.name: Very loud weapons draw patrols · Terminids, Illuminate, 1 or 2 players, peril 28+
rules.say: This weapon is heard further than most and can start breaches and Watcher alerts from far away. With 1 or 2 players, nobody covers you while you deal with it.
rules.source: The game's own noise template for each weapon. helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth: every faction detects by sound, then sight.
rules.judgement: Six tenths of the Automaton rule, like the other stealth rules on these fronts.

rules.name: Stealth advised · storms, Automatons, 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: A storm reduces line of sight for both sides. With a silenced weapon, enemies are less likely to find you.
rules.judgement: Adds to the plain stealth rule, so a storm is worth a little extra.

rules.name: Stealth helps · storms, Terminids, Illuminate, 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: A storm reduces line of sight for both sides. With a silenced weapon, enemies are less likely to find you.
rules.judgement: Adds to the plain stealth rule. Six tenths of the Automaton rule, like the other stealth rules on these fronts.

rules.name: Stealth helps · Terminids, Illuminate, 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: Terminids and Illuminate also find you by sound and sight, so a silenced weapon avoids some breaches and Watcher alerts. It matters less than against Automatons.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth: every faction detects by sound, then sight. Terminids open a breach and the Illuminate need a Watcher to call for help, and both can be interrupted.
rules.judgement: About six tenths of the Automaton rule: stealth matters most against the Automatons.

rules.name: Stealth armour advised · Automatons, 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: This armour makes you quieter or harder to spot, so fewer patrols find you.
rules.source: The passives' own effects: Reduced Signature halves movement noise and cuts detection range by 40%, Scout cuts the range, Feet First the noise.
rules.judgement: 1 or 2 players only: solo from Suicide Mission, 2 players from Impossible, growing to nearly a tier for 1 player on Super Helldive. All three passives get the same points; the community tier already orders them.

rules.name: Stealth armour helps · Terminids, Illuminate, 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: Terminids and Illuminate also find you by sound and sight. This armour matters less here than against Automatons.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stealth
rules.judgement: Six tenths of the Automaton rule, like the silenced weapon rules.

rules.name: Stealth armour not needed · peril 0 or less
rules.say: At this peril, being seen or heard costs little. A passive for survival or ammo does more.
rules.judgement: Only at peril 0 or less, such as 4 players on Challenging or 1 player on Easy. Never more than half a tier.

rules.name: Reinforcement boosters not allowed · Commando
rules.say: The game does not allow reinforcement boosters on Commando missions, so this slot does nothing.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions

rules.name: Short cooldown stratagems less useful · Commando
rules.say: Stratagems work only while the Super Destroyer is overhead, twice at most. This one is rated for its short cooldown, which barely matters here.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions

rules.name: Long cooldown stratagems help · Commando
rules.say: Stratagems work only while the Super Destroyer is overhead, twice at most, so a long cooldown costs nothing. What counts is how hard this hits.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions

rules.name: Expendable launchers less useful · Commando
rules.say: Expendable launchers are rated for being called again every minute. Here the Super Destroyer is overhead twice at most.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions

rules.name: Heat weapons help · Commando
rules.say: Resupply is a stratagem, so it comes twice at most here. This weapon runs on heat and never runs out of ammo.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions
rules.judgement: Running short of ammo follows from resupply being a stratagem. Rating a weapon that needs none a full tier higher is our judgement: the Quasar is S+ on these missions.

rules.name: Arc weapons help · Commando
rules.say: Resupply is a stratagem, so it comes twice at most here. Arc weapons use no ammo at all.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions
rules.judgement: Running short of ammo follows from resupply being a stratagem. Rating a weapon that needs none a full tier higher is our judgement: the Quasar is S+ on these missions.

rules.name: Bringing your own supplies helps · Commando
rules.say: Resupply is a stratagem, so it comes twice at most here. Supplies you bring make up for the missing resupplies.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions
rules.judgement: Named by hand: no published stat marks an item as carrying supplies.

rules.name: Silenced weapons help · Commando
rules.say: Each bot that calls for help raises the threat level across the map. A silenced weapon is heard at 13 metres instead of 100.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions

rules.name: Stealth armour helps · Commando
rules.say: Each bot that calls for help raises the threat level across the map. This armour makes you harder to find.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Commando Missions

rules.name: Silenced weapon needs stealth armour · 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: Nobody hears the shot, but patrols can still see you. Without stealth armour, the silencer helps much less.
rules.judgement: Go fully quiet or not at all. Only where stealth pays: solo from Suicide Mission, or 2 players from Impossible.

rules.name: Stealth armour helps a silenced weapon · 1 or 2 players, peril 22+
rules.say: The armour keeps patrols from finding you. The silenced weapon kills the ones you pick without alerting the rest.
rules.judgement: The other half of the same judgement, in the same range.

rules.name: True Grit shortens a long support reload
rules.say: This takes 3.5 seconds or more to reload. True Grit cuts that by 30% every time.
rules.source: Reload times from each weapon's wiki infobox. True Grit: +30% support weapon reload speed.
rules.judgement: Magazines over 120 are left out (Stalwart, Machine Gun, Flamethrower): they reload too rarely for it to show. Heat weapons are left out too: the Laser Cannon rarely swaps its heat sink.

rules.name: True Grit shortens a stationary reload
rules.say: You cannot move while this reloads. True Grit cuts that time by 30%.
rules.source: Stationary Reload, from the weapon's wiki infobox or the game's own tag.
rules.judgement: Adds to the long reload rule: a long reload you cannot move during is worse than either alone.

rules.name: True Grit shortens a reload after every shot
rules.say: This reloads after every shot, so 30% faster reloads means close to 30% more shots.
rules.source: Magazine size and reload time from the wiki.
rules.judgement: This covers the Railgun and the Speargun: short reloads, but one after every shot.

rules.name: True Grit shortens a rare long reload
rules.say: This reloads rarely, but each reload takes 3.5 seconds or more. True Grit cuts that by 30%.
rules.source: Reload times and magazine sizes from each weapon's wiki infobox. True Grit: +30% support weapon reload speed.
rules.judgement: A third of the long reload rule, because a big belt reloads rarely. Adds to the stationary rule, which puts the Machine Gun above the Stalwart.

rules.name: True Grit helps · slow support weapon reload
rules.say: Your support weapon has a long, frequent or stationary reload. True Grit cuts each one by 30%.
rules.judgement: Our own pairing.

rules.name: True Grit's reload bonus unused · no reloading support weapon
rules.say: No support weapon here reloads, so True Grit's +30% support reload does nothing. Only its +20 handling applies.
rules.judgement: Our own pairing.

rules.name: Pistol handles better · Gunslinger
rules.say: Gunslinger reloads this 40% faster, draws it 50% faster and cuts its recoil by 70%.
rules.judgement: Pistols only. The Ultimatum, Grenade Pistol and Stim Pistol are single shot tools.

rules.name: Gunslinger helps · pistol in the build
rules.say: Every part of Gunslinger improves your pistol: reload, draw speed and recoil.
rules.judgement: Our own pairing.

rules.name: Gunslinger unused · no pistol in the build
rules.say: Every part of Gunslinger is for a pistol. A launcher, the Stim Pistol or a melee weapon gets almost nothing from it.
rules.judgement: Our own pairing.

rules.name: Melee weapon hits harder · melee armour
rules.say: Your armour adds damage to every melee hit with this.
rules.judgement: Scales with the armour's melee bonus: Peak Physique and Rock Solid add 40%, Reinforced Epaulettes 20%.

rules.name: Melee armour helps · melee weapon in the build
rules.say: This passive adds melee damage, and the build has a melee weapon to use it on.
rules.judgement: Scales with the bonus. No penalty without a melee weapon: anyone can melee, and Peak Physique's ergonomics help any gun.

rules.name: Fire resistance helps · your own fire
rules.say: Fire spreads, including to where you stand. This armour cuts fire damage to you.
rules.source: The passive's own effect: Inflammable 75%, Kinetic Displacement Mitigation and Acclimated 50%, Desert Stormer 40%.
rules.judgement: Scales with the resistance, so a passive for one element beats a lower figure for all of them.

rules.name: Fire gear safer · fire resistant armour
rules.say: Fire spreads, including to where you stand. Your armour resists fire damage.
rules.judgement: Kept small: the armour only makes the weapon's downside cheaper. Scales with the armour's figure.

rules.name: Arc resistance helps · your own arc
rules.say: Arc jumps to the nearest target, you included, and a Tesla Tower most of all. This armour cuts arc damage to you.
rules.source: The passive's own effect: Electrical Conduit 95%, Adreno-Defibrillator and Acclimated 50%, Desert Stormer 40%.
rules.judgement: Scales with the resistance, so a passive for one element beats a lower figure for all of them.

rules.name: Arc gear safer · arc resistant armour
rules.say: Arc can jump to you. Your armour resists arc damage.
rules.judgement: Kept small: the armour only makes the weapon's downside cheaper. Scales with the armour's figure.

rules.name: Gas resistance helps · your own gas
rules.say: Gas damages everyone, Helldivers included. This armour cuts gas damage to you.
rules.source: The passive's own effect: Advanced Filtration 80%, Acclimated 50%, Desert Stormer 40%, Hazmat 25%.
rules.judgement: Scales with the resistance, so a passive for one element beats a lower figure for all of them.

rules.name: Gas gear safer · gas resistant armour
rules.say: Gas damages everyone, Helldivers included. Your armour resists gas damage.
rules.judgement: Kept small: the armour only makes the weapon's downside cheaper. Scales with the armour's figure.

rules.name: C4 thrown further · throw range armour
rules.say: This armour throws further, so the C4 lands further from you and closer to the target.
rules.judgement: Named by hand: nothing else is a backpack of thrown charges.

rules.name: Throw range helps · C4 Pack in the build
rules.say: This passive throws further, and the C4 Pack is full of things to throw.
rules.judgement: Servo-Assisted throws 30% further, Desert Stormer 20%.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement helps · wet or snowy ground
rules.say: Water, mud, undergrowth and snow slow you down. This booster removes most of that slowdown.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement: reduces the slow from water, snow, mud, foliage, sandstorms, blizzards and barbed wire.
rules.judgement: The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement helps · sandstorms, blizzards
rules.say: Sandstorms and blizzards slow you down. This booster removes that slowdown.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement, and the hazard text: both storms reduce mobility.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement not needed · dry ground, no storm
rules.say: Dry, firm ground and no storm, so this booster has nothing to do.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement: no effect on dry sand without weather, slopes, vaulting or tremors.
rules.judgement: The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: Muscle Enhancement less useful · dry ground, Terminids
rules.say: Dry ground and no storm, so the terrain half does nothing. It still shortens the slow from bug acid.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Muscle Enhancement: also covers the slow from Terminid acid and Bug Mine explosions.
rules.judgement: The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: Jump Pack helps · steep ground
rules.say: The Jump Pack's landing cancels fall damage, so you can drop off cliffs safely.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, LIFT-850 Jump Pack: no fall damage when the landing thrusters fire.
rules.judgement: The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: Warp Pack risky · steep ground
rules.say: The Warp Pack moves you 10 metres straight ahead, even into mid-air, and nothing breaks the fall.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, LIFT-182 Warp Pack: warping in mid-air leaves you in mid-air, and the fall can hurt.
rules.judgement: The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: FRVs help · flat, open ground
rules.say: Flat, open ground. The FRV drives fastest here and rarely flips.
rules.judgement: From play: an oasis map drove easily. The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: FRVs flip easily · rough ground
rules.say: On broken, rocky or icy ground the FRV flips on ledges, and you end up walking.
rules.judgement: From play: snow, volcanic, rocky canyon and highland planets drive badly, and players on Steam agree. The ground for each biome is our own reading.

rules.name: Jump Pack risky · megacity planet
rules.say: This planet has a megacity, so you may fight between buildings. Hitting one mid-jump ragdolls you.
rules.judgement: From play. Some players prefer fighting from rooftops instead. Counts half: a megacity on the planet does not mean your mission is in it.

rules.name: Warp Pack helps · megacity planet
rules.say: This planet has a megacity, so you may fight between buildings. The Warp Pack goes through walls.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, LIFT-182 Warp Pack: passes through terrain, buildings, enemies and bunker doors.
rules.judgement: Counts half: a megacity on the planet does not mean your mission is in it.

rules.name: Warp Pack helps · 1 player
rules.say: Alone, you cannot open two person bunker doors. The Warp Pack goes straight through them.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Bunker: two Helldivers press a button each, or one uses the Warp Pack.

rules.name: Orbital Laser helps · missions of 15 minutes or less
rules.say: It has 3 uses, 5 minutes apart. On a mission this short you use all 3, each on a base.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Orbital Laser: 3 uses, 300 second cooldown. Mission time limits from each mission's article.
rules.judgement: On a short mission you get the most from all 3 uses. On a 40 minute mission they are gone halfway through.

rules.name: Stamina Enhancement helps · intense heat
rules.say: Intense heat halves your stamina. This booster gives back a good part of it.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stamina Enhancement: +22.5% max stamina and +40% regen; Intense Heat halves max stamina

rules.name: Integrated Extinguishers help · fire tornadoes, volcanic activity
rules.say: This planet sets Helldivers on fire. This booster puts you out sooner.
rules.source: The booster's own text, and the hazard text: fire tornadoes, and burning rocks from volcanoes.
rules.judgement: Our own reading of the hazards.

rules.name: Shield Generator Pack helps · acid storms, sandstorms, blizzards
rules.say: While it holds, the bubble keeps out acid storms, sandstorms and blizzards. It does not block fire or gas.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, SH-32 Shield Generator Pack: blocks blizzards, sandstorms, acid storms and acid splash; not fire or gas

rules.name: Integrated Extinguishers help · your own fire
rules.say: Fire spreads, including to where you stand. This booster puts you out faster.
rules.source: The booster's own text
rules.judgement: Throwables do not count: a thermite grenade is anti-tank.

rules.name: Explosive resistance helps · your own close blasts
rules.say: Something in this build explodes close to you. Helldivers already take half explosion damage, and this armour reduces it further.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg: Helldivers take 50% of explosion damage. The passive's own effect.
rules.judgement: The close blast tag is ours: nothing published marks a weapon you set off close.

rules.name: Close blasts safer · explosive resistant armour
rules.say: Your armour reduces damage from your own explosions, so you can use this closer.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg: Helldivers take 50% of explosion damage
rules.judgement: Through our close blast tag.

rules.name: Faster primary reload helps · slow reloading primary
rules.say: Your primary reloads slowly or one shell at a time. This armour speeds that up.
rules.source: The passive's own effect. Reload times from each weapon's wiki infobox
rules.judgement: Slow means 3.6 seconds or more, a round by round reload, a shotgun, or a magazine of 6 or fewer with a reload of 3 seconds or more.

rules.name: Slow reload shortened · primary reload armour
rules.say: This weapon reloads slowly. Your armour speeds up its reload.
rules.judgement: The mirror of the rule above.

rules.name: Crouched recoil reduction helps · weapon fired crouched
rules.say: Your build has a weapon you fire crouched or prone, and this armour cuts recoil in those stances.
rules.source: The passive's own effect: -30% recoil crouched or prone
rules.judgement: Tentative. The weapons are named by hand.

rules.name: Vitality Enhancement helps · gas resistant armour
rules.say: Your armour resists most gas, and this booster adds more resistance. Together you can stand in your own gas.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Orbital Gas Strike: Advanced Filtration with Vitality Enhancement makes a Helldiver immune to gas
rules.judgement: Our own pairing.

rules.name: Stim Pistol helps · armour that lengthens stims
rules.say: Your armour adds 2 seconds to every stim, including the ones this pistol fires at your squad.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Med-Kit: the longer stim duration extends to the P-11 Stim Pistol

rules.name: Longer stims help · Stim Pistol in the build
rules.say: With the Stim Pistol, the 2 extra seconds on every stim reach your squad too.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Med-Kit

rules.name: Ballistic Shield helps · one handed primary
rules.say: The shield takes one hand and your primary needs only one, so you can fire from behind the shield.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Ballistic Shield Backpack: it needs a weapon with the One Handed trait. The trait from each weapon's infobox

rules.name: Ballistic Shield less useful · two handed primary
rules.say: The shield takes one hand and your primary needs two, so behind the shield you fight with your sidearm.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Ballistic Shield Backpack
rules.judgement: Also applies when the build has no primary yet.

rules.name: One handed primary helps · Ballistic Shield in the build
rules.say: You can fire this with one hand while holding the shield in the other.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Ballistic Shield Backpack

rules.name: Stamina Enhancement helps · heavy armour
rules.say: Heavy armour recovers stamina at half the rate of medium. This booster gives a lot of that back.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stamina Enhancement: +22.5% max stamina, +40% regen. Armour: heavy regen 50, medium 100.
rules.judgement: Our own pairing. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Dead Sprint helps · heavy armour
rules.say: Heavy armour runs out of stamina first. Dead Sprint lets you keep running at the cost of health.
rules.judgement: Heavy armour needs help with stamina. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Jump or Warp Pack helps · heavy armour
rules.say: Heavy armour is the slowest weight. This pack covers ground faster than you can run.
rules.judgement: Our own pairing. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Shield Generator Pack helps · light armour
rules.say: Light armour has a low armour rating. The bubble blocks the first 150 damage from any direction.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, SH-32 Shield Generator Pack: 150 shield health, 360 degrees
rules.judgement: Our own pairing. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Heavy armour helps · Automatons
rules.say: Automatons mostly shoot. Heavy armour takes small arms fire and stray rockets better.
rules.judgement: Community advice from Steam: heavy for Automatons, light for Terminids, medium either way. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Heavy armour less useful · Terminids
rules.say: Against Terminids you survive by dodging, and heavy armour is too slow for that. Spewers and Bile Titans hit hard through any armour rating.
rules.judgement: Community advice from Steam. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Light armour helps · Terminids
rules.say: Terminids attack up close. Light armour is the fastest weight.
rules.judgement: Community advice from Steam, and a survey of 304 missions in which 70% of players wore light. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Heavy armour less useful · intense heat
rules.say: Intense heat halves your stamina, and heavy armour already recovers it at half the medium rate.
rules.source: helldivers.wiki.gg, Stamina Enhancement: Intense Heat halves max stamina
rules.judgement: Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

rules.name: Sentries and emplacements help · heavy armour
rules.say: Heavy armour suits holding one position, which is where sentries and emplacements work best.
rules.judgement: From a survey of 304 missions: three quarters of heavy armour players brought 3 turrets. A small effect. Needs a chosen armour set, for its weight.

knownGaps: Three visibility rules lean on a long-range tag that is our judgement rather than a published field. It lives in vocabulary.json with its reasoning, and the rules that read it carry a `judgement` saying so. It used to be the same six ids written out inside each of those three rules.

The visibility rules key on the Marksman category only. Special was tried and dropped: it holds a flamethrower, a stim pistol and a shotgun pistol alongside the Dominator, so it says nothing about range.

Armour penetration moves no rating at the item level and it must not. It moves one at the loadout level as of 1.20.0: build-rules.json reads the best thing a build holds against the front, which splits the 39 curated builds 36 / 41 / 23 where the per item reading split 51 primaries 48 to 3. Enemy armour is still shown on every expanded row as a fact. See whyThereAreNoArmourRules, which is about this file and stays true.

Suppressed is sourced from a wiki article infobox rather than from a module, so it is curated on the items instead of fetched. It is a real published fact, 13 metres of audible range on the wiki's Stealth page, and it carries no `judgement` field for that reason. fetch-wiki.mjs reads weapon infoboxes since 4 October 2026, for reload times, so moving Suppressed into the fetch is now a small change rather than a new one.

The weather rules price a hazard as if it were always happening. A planet listing sandstorms has sandstorms sometimes, roughly three minutes at a time, and nothing in the data says how often. The visibility penalties are set as a risk you carry across a run rather than a state you are in, which is a judgement and not a measurement.

Peril is 6 * (difficulty - 5) + SQUAD_PRESSURE[squad], where the squad curve is [10, 4, 1, 0] taken from the wiki patrol interval multipliers. The formula is unchanged on 4 October 2026; what changed is that the stealth rules also gate on squad. The curator: a four stack on Super Helldive knows what it is doing, so stealth is a question for one or two of you, from solo on Suicide Mission or two of you on Impossible. Peril alone puts four of you at difficulty 10 above two of you at 9, which is the wrong way round for stealth, so the squad gate does what the formula cannot.

The stealth rules scale off peril from 16, gated at 22, for one or two of you. Bugs and squids have their own, at about six tenths of the bot figure, since 4 October 2026. Nothing on bugs or squids reads difficulty for anything but stealth, so the gradient there is still thin.

The negative half is used once. easy-drop-wastes-stealth-armour takes up to half a tier off stealth passives below zero peril. The old inverted halves, silenced weapons marked down and loud ones lifted on an easy drop, were removed on 4 October 2026: not needing stealth is not a reason to mark it down. Nothing yet says that anti tank at difficulty 3 is firepower for an enemy that does not spawn.

A rule scaling off peril must not name a squad size in its say. Peril is 6 * (difficulty - 5) + SQUAD_PRESSURE[squad] and depth reaches it as readily as being alone does, so four players on Super Helldive sit at 30. All three bot peril rules shipped in 1.19.0 asserting the reader was outnumbered, and their inverted halves asserted the reader was not, both on a figure that says neither. Fixed on 22 August 2026 by describing the pressure instead. Nothing about how a squad size might get its own wording is solved here; the rule simply may not claim one it did not check.

Pairing rules, those with an alongside or notAlongside clause, read the rest of the build and so never fire on a tier row. They show in the builder's picker and slots and on every build's parts. Twenty since 4 October 2026: stealth, True Grit, Gunslinger, melee, fire, arc and gas resistance, and C4 with throw range. npm run builds measures them by placing each subject in 60 random builds.

Considered and cut by the curator on 4 October 2026, recorded so nobody rebuilds them. True Grit worth more solo, and team weapons marked down solo: the wiki says assisted reloads skip True Grit and team weapons are built for a loader, but in practice nobody team reloads, so neither changes what is worth bringing. Peak Physique paired with low ergonomics support weapons: the +30 ergonomics is real, but those weapons are better served by other passives. Kinetic Displacement or Blunt Force Mitigation paired with a Jump Pack or a vehicle: nobody should pick a passive to soften their own bad landings.

Held back for want of a source, 4 October 2026: whether Med-Kit's longer stims also lengthen Experimental Infusion, whether Localization Confusion matters more for a small squad, and how the Hover Pack fares on steep ground. Fire against the Automatons is not a gap: the wiki gives no front wide fire resistance, and the vote already prices flame's short range against a front that shoots from far away.

The city rules guess from the planet: a planet with a megacity reads as a city fight wherever the mission actually is. The scenario does not know which part of a planet a mission is on, so those rules carry half weight and say they are a guess.

Armour weight comes from the set a build wears, since 4 October 2026, and every build made before then, and every preset, has no set and so no weight. The weight rules stay silent on those rather than guessing medium, the same contract as an unset difficulty.
